title: Last European trip in 1970
summary: He was sent for by John Dow, stayed six to eight weeks, and was featured in a local band.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Now from there, in 1970 you went back to Europe. Who did you go to Europe with in 1970? It's in your passport, the last time that you were in Europe.
The last time I went it was with John Dow.)
Oh, again, two times you were there.
He sent for him. John (Dow) always sent for him.
He never went with a group. His sister and I took him to the airport, his sister over there. He filled in for what's-his-name, was supposed to go and he was sick and couldn't go...
Who was that?
Who was the musician that couldn't go and he sent for you to fill his place? When you went one time to Europe, when they sent for you? Who was the musician?
Sent for me?
He couldn't go. The other musician was sick and couldn't go so you went in his place, Jay. Who is he?
I don't remember that one. I don't remember nobody sending for me but John Hammond.
I said this musician could not go because he was sick. But you didn't stay long. Oh, I know his name and I can't call it.
We'll think about that. No problem. When you went to Europe this last time, how long did you stay about?
I stayed about 6 or 8 weeks.
It's on his passport.
And you worked pretty much the whole time you were there? You didn't have any time off?
Yeah, I did pretty good.
Working as a single, by yourself?
No, with the band. See, they had their own band over there. They featured me in the band. Just playing whenever you get ready.
Do you remember about how much money you were making a week?
I made a little.
A little bit or a lot?
They say it's a whole lot over there.
How much is a whole lot over there?
Now you're talking. I made it all right. All expenses paid, all the food, and I had my little bottle, didn't get drunk and did my work, period.
